answer.exemplar: Assign a probability to each outcome so they sum to 1, then add the probabilities of the outcomes in the event.

questions.explanation: Non-uniform spaces require explicit probabilities. Counting favorable outcomes no longer suffices.

options.text: Only if the sample is large.

questions.explanation: Some assumptions depend on how data were collected, not on the data values. Study design must justify them.

Fixed n independent trials with two outcomes and constant p.

questions.explanation: Binomial requires fixed n, independence, two outcomes, and constant p. Changing p or dependence breaks it.

questions.topic: Type one and type two errors

options.text: Type I error is a correct decision.

options.misconception: confuses type I and type II

options.text: Type I error is accepting the null.

questions.explanation: Type I error is rejecting a true null; type II is failing to reject a false null. The clerk swapped them.

questions.explanation: Power is the probability of correctly rejecting a false null. It equals 1 minus type II error probability.
